Karthik / Monica — reviewed HealthNexana's redlines and inventory. High level comments below; attached is a draft "counsel_comments" doc with suggested language we can propose as round 2.

1) Cross-border transfers / SCCs
- Acceptable: Redwood will execute SCCs for EU controller-to-processor flows. Proposed insertion: "Parties shall rely on the European Commission’s Standard Contractual Clauses (processor-to-controller or controller-to-processor as required) and the Transfer Addendum (Annex X)".
- Note: For telemetry/usage metadata exported for product analytics we will apply pseudonymization where feasible and maintain encryption-at-rest. We cannot commit to customer-side encryption keys for hosted plans without Dedicated/Private deployment terms.

2) Subprocessor notice window
- Company's ask of 30 days is operationally challenging for infra/backplane updates. Proposed compromise: 15 calendar days written notice with an objection right limited to reasonable security/privacy grounds; if objected, parties will seek to resolve in good faith and Customer's continued use of the service for 30 days constitutes deemed consent unless a specific mitigation is agreed.

3) Audit & attestation
- SOC 2 Type II report (annual) will be provided upon NDA/procurement channel. For event-driven audits, we will offer a scoped right limited to the incident and forensics; customer bears reasonable costs unless Redwood is at fault.

4) Liability cap / indemnity notes
- Redlines increasing caps to unlimited liability are unacceptable. We can provide carve-outs for willful misconduct and gross negligence. Recommend preserving mutual indemnities but limit cap to the greater of: (i) fees paid in prior 12 months, or (ii) $1M.

5) E-Sign & execution path
- DocuSign preferred. I recommend we prepare a redline-merged version, confirm final language, and then generate a single DocuSign envelope. Ops can route signing order: HealthNexana -> Redwood legal -> Account exec.

Attached: RDW_counsel_comments_v1.docx (Word, 24KB) — contains line-by-line suggestions.

Markus Klein
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
Legal & Privacy
